comments.author: Dana Whitfield
comments.body: Proposal: inject env into the key and migrate production to DB 2 this week — need a brief dual-write window.

content.text: Proposal: inject env into the key and migrate production to DB 2 this week — need a brief dual-write window.

Staging and production API clusters share a Redis logical database for historical reasons and form rate-limit keys as rl:{api_key_hash}:{window}. A load test in staging that exhausts a key hash identical to a production token shape can throttle real traffic if the hash collides, and staging resets have cleared production counters overnight.
Keys must be cluster-scoped (e.g. rl:{env}:{api_key_hash}:{window}) or use separate Redis DBs. Today neither env var RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX nor the deployment name is folded into the key material.

During last Thursday's staging soak we observed production 429 rates jump ~3x for tokens whose SHA-256 prefix matched fixtures in the load script. No data corruption, but customer-facing throttling from a non-prod workload is unacceptable.
